newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek shares slide in nervous pre-election trade.
newsitem.headline: Greek shares slide in nervous pre-election trade.

text.p: Greek equities traded in negative territory on lower volume as profit taking continued for the third straight session. Brokers said there was a feeling of nervousness in the market ahead of the national vote on Sunday.

"Profit taking continued on Thursday as players opted to reduce risk ahead of the elections on Sunday. The market's advance had been supported by the expectation of a strong socialist lead but recent polls are casting doubt on this," said Alexander Moraitakis, managing director of Nuntius Securities.

"With conflicting polls on the election outcome the prudent trading tactic is to take some of the profits after the recent rally. But whatever party wins, the market's prospects are positive. New Democracy has promised tax incentive measures to boost the stock market," he said.

Another floor trader noted that the market's recent climb was psychologically driven and had less to do with concrete reasons. There was a bit of nervousness, three days before national polls and a good amount of selling by certain funds.
Greece will hold early elections September 22.

The Athens general share index closed 0.21 percent, or 1.98 points lower at 961.49 from Wednesday's 963.47 close after opening at 964.09 points. Turnover fell to 7.9 billion drachmas from 10 billion on Wednesday on volume of 4.09 million shares.
Losers led gainers 130 to 90 with 16 issues unchanged on 236 traded. Banks slipped 0.31 percent, industrials eased 0.56 percent and construction eased 0.03 percent. Small-caps fell by 0.79 percent.
